title: coyodex
goal: coyodex is for a developer whose AI coding agent has generated more code than they can hold in their head — the point where the project still runs but nobody knows what is under it (the "Coyote Effect"). It gives that developer a top-down, drillable map of their own repo: a behavioral layer (goal, roles, use cases, one ordered Happy Path) over a structural layer (subsystems, components, dependencies, a domain model, and per-use-case flows), where every box and arrow is written in plain language and anchored to a real file:line. The map is not a drawing: it is a JSON model committed next to the code and pinned to a commit, produced by a coding agent following a written method, checked by deterministic tools (schema + semantics, self-contradiction, diagram balance, anchor grounding), rendered as a committed markdown view, and served live as an interactive C4 viewer. When the code changes, the same tools project the diff onto the map, show what it ripples to, and fold the result back into the baseline — so the map stays in step with the code instead of rotting.

roles.name: Developer
roles.wants: to understand and oversee a codebase their coding agent generated — see what it does top-down, drill to the code only where needed, and keep that picture true as the code moves
roles.drives: UC1, UC10, UC11, UC12, UC13, UC15, UC17

roles.name: Coding agent
roles.wants: to follow the coyodex method and produce a map that is well-formed, self-consistent and grounded in the code — and to be told, mechanically, wherever it is not
roles.drives: UC2, UC3, UC4, UC5, UC6, UC7, UC8, UC9, UC14, UC16

roles.name: Method maintainer
roles.wants: to know whether a change to the method or the tools makes the maps they produce better or worse, before shipping it

use_cases.name: Install the coyodex skill
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Runs `make install` in the coyodex clone → a repo-local virtualenv holds the `coyodex` CLI, and each agent's skills home holds a SKILL.md with this clone's absolute path baked in, so `/coyodex` works from any project.

use_cases.name: Pre-index the repo
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Runs `coyodex preindex` before the structural harvest → `.coyodex/preindex.json` holds the directory weight tree, the symbol index, the component expectation E per slice, and an honest list of what could not be parsed; a one-line summary lands on stderr.

use_cases.name: Self-check a build fragment
use_cases.trigger_outcome: A harvest or trace agent runs `coyodex lint-fragment` on its own fragment before returning → every schema, anchor-format, unknown-key and missing-file error is reported in that agent's own turn, so nothing bounces back from the lead's assemble.

use_cases.name: Assemble the map from fragments
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Runs `coyodex assemble <fragments> --out .coyodex --reconcile …` → the fragments merge into one canonical `project-map.json` plus its markdown view, with duplicate deps/components collapsed, actor edges stripped, missing C→E edges derived, and the reconcile assignments applied.

use_cases.name: Validate the map
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Runs `coyodex validate --check-sources --check-coverage` → blocking problems (dangling references, malformed anchors, unwitnessed edges, a stale committed view) and advisory nudges are printed, and the exit code says whether the map is well-formed.

use_cases.name: Audit the map for self-contradiction
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Runs `coyodex audit` → the narrative Happy Path and the mechanism (flows + edges) are made to refute each other, blocking only on a hard `why:` contradiction, and the ranked L2 grounding worklist is printed for fresh-context skeptics.

use_cases.name: Correct drifted anchors
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Feeds the skeptics' verdicts to `coyodex anchor-drift`, then `coyodex fix apply-drift` → every confirmed claim whose stored anchor sits far from the line the skeptics actually found is rewritten to that line, matched on the full edge triple.

use_cases.name: Re-balance the map's grouping
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Runs `coyodex balance` after the trace → every diagram's fan-out, the inter-subsystem edge matrix, and a deterministic split proposal for each over-dense screen, printed as Direct-map-change blocks to accept or justify.

use_cases.name: Render the committed markdown view
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Runs `coyodex render project-map.json project-map.md` → the readable markdown view is regenerated from the model in canonical order, and the project is registered so it appears on the map server's landing page.

use_cases.name: Serve the maps
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Runs `make start` once → a local server listens on 127.0.0.1:8765 and its landing page lists every project already opened, each openable, removable and reorderable; new folders are added by browsing to them.

use_cases.name: Explore a map in the viewer
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Opens `/p/<project>/` → the frontend fetches the whole view bundle and draws the Context, Subsystems, Domain, Deployment, Happy-Path and flow diagrams, each box drillable into the level below and selectable for its plain-language explanation.

use_cases.name: Read a mapped element's source
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Clicks an element's source link in the viewer → the file is shown at the map's own commit in the built-in code viewer, positioned at the anchored line, with a hand-off to the local editor or GitHub when a local file is wanted.

use_cases.name: Explore the impact of a code change
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Picks a base and a target in the viewer's impact explorer → the diff is projected onto the map's anchors, each hit labelled with how precisely it resolved (line, symbol or file), and the elements it ripples to are badged on the diagrams.

use_cases.name: Accept a change into the baseline
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Patches the model for the reviewed change → the map's fields are edited surgically, the pin is bumped to the new commit, provenance is re-stamped with this conversation, and the gates re-run before the map is committed with the code.

use_cases.name: Ask for a direct map change
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Asks in plain language to move, rename, split or group something → the agent edits the model surgically, stays inside what the code actually backs, re-runs validate → audit → render, and commits the result.

use_cases.name: Look up an element in the model
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Runs `coyodex dump --id/--record/--edges/--members` → that element's kind, name, canonical source, full stored record, incident backbone edges or group members come back as JSON, without opening the whole map.

use_cases.name: Back up a map with its conversation
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Runs `map_backup.py backup <repo>` → the stamped provenance is read and the map files are bundled with the exact conversation transcripts that produced them, under a dated folder in the coyodex clone.

use_cases.name: Run the method-quality eval
use_cases.trigger_outcome: Runs `coyodex-eval run` on a freshly built map → its deterministic profile and judge report are compared against the blessed baseline, and the verdict is PASS, DRIFT or REGRESSED with the tripped gate named.

subsystems.name: Map model
subsystems.purpose: The committed JSON model every other part reads and writes, plus the vocabulary it is written in — element ids, dependency kinds and purpose buckets, entry-point kinds, edge-verb families, domain-relation verbs, and the one canonical source-anchor format.

subsystems.name: Map authoring
subsystems.purpose: Turning a codebase into a map: sizing and locating the code before the harvest, letting each build agent self-check its own fragment, merging the fragments into the canonical model, and recording which conversation produced it.

subsystems.name: Map verification
subsystems.purpose: The gates a written map must pass: is it well-formed, does it contradict itself, are its diagrams readable, and do its claims still point at the lines where the work actually happens.

subsystems.name: Map viewer
subsystems.purpose: Showing a map: a local server that pins every file read to the map's own commit, the builder that turns the model into every diagram the frontend draws, the generated markdown view, and the browser page the developer drills.

subsystems.name: Change impact
subsystems.purpose: Answering "what did my commit touch on the map": projecting an arbitrary git diff onto the map's anchors in the pin's line frame, then spreading from the elements it hit directly to the ones they reach.

subsystems.name: Method-quality eval
subsystems.purpose: Guarding the method itself: reducing a built map to comparable numbers, adding the semantic scores no deterministic check can see, and gating a rebuild against the blessed baseline so a method change that made maps worse is caught.

subsystems.name: Method & command entry
subsystems.purpose: How coyodex reaches its users: the written method a coding agent follows, the skill manifests installed into each agent's skills home, and the single command that routes every tool verb.

components.name: Map model & serializer
components.purpose: Defines the map as typed dataclasses, loads a JSON document into them while reporting the exact JSON path of any shape violation, and writes it back through one deterministic serializer so the committed file always diffs cleanly. Also generates the documentation-only JSON Schema straight from the same dataclasses, so the two cannot drift.
components.depends_on: the shared grammar for id tokens and verb families

evidence.why: load_model is the structural half of `coyodex validate` — parse, then field-by-field type check
to_canonical_json is the one serialization: fixed key order, indent 2, so the same model is byte-identical
remap_element_ids rewrites every reference when a merge collapses one element id into another

components.name: Shared grammar & anchors
components.purpose: The single place every reader agrees on meaning: which id shapes exist, how a dependency's kind and purpose bucket are classified, how an entry-point kind folds to its seed and what activation it implies, what each backbone verb reveals about a dependency's role, which domain-relation verb is canonical, and what a source anchor may look like.
components.depends_on: nothing inside coyodex — anchors deliberately imports no coyodex module

evidence.why: edge_role maps a backbone verb to the role it reveals — the derivation behind a dependency's shown role
canonical_entry_kind is the one normalizer every consumer routes an entry-point kind through
anchor_drift is the deterministic judge of whether a stored anchor drifted from the reported line

components.name: Model reader
components.purpose: Read-only lookups over a written map, for orchestration glue and change-impact spelunking: the whole model as JSON, or one of a deliberately tiny fixed set of slices — an id resolved to its kind, name and source; an element's full stored record; the backbone edges into and out of a node; a group's members.
components.depends_on: the map model loader

evidence.why: the slice surface is fixed on purpose — this is a reader, not a query language

components.name: Structural pre-index
components.purpose: Sizes and locates a codebase before anyone names a component: a directory tree weighted by lines, file count and git churn; a symbol index resolving names to definitions with their extents; a lower-bound import-edge advisory between components the agent already named; the code-derived component expectation E per directory; and an honest record of every file it could not parse.
components.depends_on: tree-sitter for non-Python symbols, git for churn

evidence.why: expected_components computes E deterministically from the code tree — the leaf-decision anchor
tree-sitter is imported lazily and its absence is reported as uncovered, never as empty

components.name: Fragment linter
components.purpose: The self-check a harvest or trace agent runs on its own fragment before returning it. It reuses the validator's checks at fragment scope — schema shape, anchor format, unknown-key conventions, entry-point kinds, edge rules — and, given the repo, confirms every anchored file really exists, so a wrong repo-root prefix dies in the agent's own turn instead of at the lead's assemble.
components.depends_on: the fragment loader and the validator's check functions

evidence.why: the whole point is moving the fix into the agent's own context, in parallel, instead of the lead patching serially

components.name: Fragment assembler
components.purpose: Merges the build agents' fragments into the one canonical model. It validates each fragment alone so a bad one fails by name, refuses a duplicate id across fragments, collapses the same dependency or module found by two slices, strips backbone edges that wrongly name an actor, derives the component-to-entity edge an entity flow-step implies but nobody wrote, applies the declarative reconcile directives, and writes the model plus its markdown view.
components.depends_on: the model serializer, the reconcile loader, the markdown view generator

evidence.why: _derive_entity_edges heals the missing C→E edge from the flow step, idempotently, on every assemble
apply_reconcile is what makes group assignments and refuted-edge drops survive a re-assemble

components.name: Provenance & backup
components.purpose: Records which conversation produced a map — session id, build minute, mode and the code commit — into a committed provenance file, and later bundles the map files together with those exact conversation transcripts into a dated backup folder. Deliberately standalone and stdlib-only so it keeps working when the project virtualenv is broken.
components.depends_on: the coding agent's local transcript store and git

evidence.why: un-stamped maps are recovered by finding transcripts that actually wrote a project-map file
transcripts are always copied, never moved — they live in the agent's live store

components.name: Model validator
components.purpose: Answers "is this map well-formed?". Past the structural load it checks the semantics: every referenced id resolves, groups nest without cycles under the right kind of parent, Happy-Path steps name their use case, flow steps carry a phrase and a call site, edges carry a witness, domain cards are complete, and — against the repo — that every anchor exists and no entity was synthesized. It also re-measures the tree for coverage and granularity advisories, and flags a committed markdown view that has gone stale.
components.depends_on: the model loader, the grammar, the balance advisories

evidence.why: check_hierarchy is the grouping check: right-kind parent, defined, no cycles
validate_model returns problems and warnings — the split between blocking and advisory

components.name: Model auditor
components.purpose: Answers "does this map contradict itself?" with no code at all, by making the map's two layers refute each other: the narrative Happy Path against the mechanism of flows and backbone edges. It blocks only on a hard prerequisite contradiction and keeps its ordering and actor checks advisory, then prints the ranked worklist of "what this actually does" claims that only a fresh-context skeptic reading the code can settle.
components.depends_on: the model, expanded flows, the grammar's verb families

evidence.why: l2_worklist_model builds the ranked grounding worklist, most dangerous first
each work item carries self-describing detail so a skeptic needs no map file

components.name: Diagram balance
components.purpose: Answers "is each screen readable?". It computes every rendered diagram's immediate-children count against the 5±2 target, honours recorded exceptions, and for an over-dense screen proposes a deterministic split — a greedy modularity partition of the component graph, or of the quotient graph one level up — while refusing to propose noise on list-shaped or star-shaped screens. It only ever re-groups; it may never merge or split a component to hit a number.
components.depends_on: the model's grouping and backbone edges

evidence.why: propose_split is the deterministic greedy proposer behind the report's suggestions
balance_warnings are the always-on advisories the validator appends

components.name: Grounding reconcile
components.purpose: Closes the grounding loop after the skeptics have read the code. It compares each confirmed claim's stored anchor against the line the skeptics reported and reports the drift deterministically, then applies the corrections to the model in place — rewriting a drifted edge or security anchor matched on the full triple, dropping a refuted edge while healing or reporting the flow steps that rode it, and resolving a duplicate domain relation by an explicit human choice.
components.depends_on: the audit worklist, the anchor drift math, the model serializer

evidence.why: apply_drift writes the corrected line, matching on the full (src, verb, dst) triple so paired edges never swap
consensus_evidence takes the median reported line, so one stray skeptic cannot move an anchor

components.name: Map server
components.purpose: The viewer's whole backend, on loopback only: it serves the generic shell and shared frontend assets, each project's view data, and a file browser plus code viewer whose reads are pinned to that map's own commit — so what you read always matches what the map describes. It scans no disk: the served set is exactly the folders the developer has opened, remembered in a small recents file that concurrent writers merge rather than clobber.
components.depends_on: git for every file read, the view bundle builder, the file tree builder

evidence.why: ensure_fresh drops the per-map caches when the model file changes, so an edited map shows on the next request
git_show is how every file the viewer displays is read — from the commit, not the working tree
register_project lets a build add itself to the landing page without importing the server

components.name: View bundle builder
components.purpose: Turns the map's graph into everything the frontend draws: the Context, Subsystems, per-subsystem, edge-card, Domain, subdomain, bridge and Deployment diagrams, the Happy-Path sequence, one sequence diagram plus a readable narrative per use-case flow, the crossing-edge lists behind each aggregated arrow, and the source-link configuration. It also holds the graph data model and the parser for a change-impact report.
components.depends_on: the graph produced from the model, git for the origin remote

evidence.why: ViewBundle is the contract between this builder and the frontend
GraphDict is the graph shape the model is converted into

components.name: Generated views
components.purpose: The pure model-to-view conversions: the committed markdown rendering in canonical section order that is never hand-edited, the graph the viewer's diagram builder consumes, and the repo's file tree tagged by how the map covers each path — so the file browser doubles as a coverage view showing what the map describes and what it misses.
components.depends_on: the model and the shared grammar only

evidence.why: model_to_graph builds the viewer's graph straight from the model, with no second grammar
build_tree tags each path self/under/has/none — the coverage overlay

components.name: Viewer frontend
components.purpose: The browser page the developer actually uses: one generic bundle for every map that fetches its project's view data at boot, renders each diagram with pan, zoom and a click-to-side-panel bridge, drills box by box down the altitudes as a back/forward history, shows the file tree and the code at the map's commit, runs the impact explorer, and hands off to the local editor or GitHub when a real file is wanted.
components.depends_on: the map server's project API, Mermaid and svg-pan-zoom from a CDN

evidence.why: all per-project data arrives from the server at boot and is assigned by applyBundle
Mermaid and svg-pan-zoom load from a pinned CDN with subresource integrity

components.name: Impact projection
components.purpose: Projects an arbitrary git diff onto the map's anchors. Because every anchor is a line at the pin, it re-expresses each changed file in the pin's frame across renames and compares the two sides' hunks to decide which of the pin's lines the change really affects, then resolves each anchor at the finest rung it can honestly claim — the line, the enclosing definition, or just the file — never faking precision.
components.depends_on: read-only git, the pre-index's symbol extents

evidence.why: FileFrame is the pin-frame effect of a change on one file — which of the pin's lines it affects
rename maps come from full-tree passes, never a single-path pathspec, which would fabricate deletes

components.name: Impact ripple
components.purpose: Spreads from the elements a change hit directly to the ones they reach — the subsystem that contains them, the use cases whose flows step through them, the entities they persist — under pinned semantics: the rules apply once from the direct hits, a rippled element never re-fires, and only an opt-in call-graph walk goes further than one hop. Each reached element keeps the strongest signal that found it. Also parses a unified diff into the rows the code view paints.
components.depends_on: the direct hits from the projection layer, the model's grouping, flows and edges

evidence.why: the strength lattice orders every cause from direct-line down to territory
RippleOptions keeps the noisy links (reads-only, entity graph, call graph) off by default

components.name: Eval harness
components.purpose: The eval's deterministic orchestration: it profiles a freshly built map, attaches a judge report, compares the pair against the blessed baseline under hard gates and softer drift bands, archives the run, and promotes a run to become the new baseline. It never builds a map and never calls a model itself, so the whole pipeline is testable without an LLM.
components.depends_on: the map profile, the judge report, the coyodex core

evidence.why: compare applies the hard gates then the bands, and the verdict precedence is REGRESSED > DRIFT > PASS
bless promotes a run directory to the baseline

components.name: Eval profile & judge
components.purpose: The two measurements a comparison needs. The profile reduces a map to signals that survive an LLM rewriting it — element counts, validator and audit outcomes, coverage flags, density, balance, and the name sets a gate can watch. The judge layer holds the seam to the model: the prompt builders and aggregation math for skeptics grounding the riskiest claims and judges scoring the rubric, with the model call itself injected.
components.depends_on: the validator and auditor for the shared parse; an injected judge for the semantic half

evidence.why: Judge is the dependency-injection boundary to the model — a fake in tests, a sub-agent in the orchestrator
majority_verdict decides a claim from N skeptics, and a failed skeptic is never counted as refuted

components.name: Method docs
components.purpose: The method itself — the prompts a coding agent follows to build and maintain a map. It fixes the deliverable sections and their order, the behavioral-before-structural rule, how to pick altitude, the harvest and trace prompts, the invariant every write must pass, and the field-by-field contract of the stored model, the domain cards and the change-impact report.
components.depends_on: the coyodex CLI verbs it prescribes

evidence.why: dispatch is the entry doc: it picks build, analyze or accept and points at every other doc
the invariant after every write is validate --check-sources, then audit, then render

components.name: Skill manifest & installer
components.purpose: The install path and the two manifests it writes. `make install` builds the repo-local virtualenv, installs both packages editable into it, and copies a SKILL.md into each agent's global skills home with this clone's absolute path substituted for the placeholder. The manifests carry no method of their own on purpose: they name the trigger phrases, separate the coyodex clone from the repo being mapped, and send the agent straight to the dispatch doc — so the method can evolve in the clone without ever reinstalling.
components.depends_on: the method docs it points at

evidence.why: the manifest is copied with __COYODEX_HOME__ replaced by this clone's absolute path
the manifest states that the repo is the source of truth and the skill only points at it
the CLI is installed editable, so the repo stays the source of truth

components.name: CLI dispatcher
components.purpose: The single `coyodex` command. It parses nothing but the verb, defaults a missing map argument to the conventional path, and imports each verb's implementation lazily inside its own branch — a deliberate dependency firewall that keeps validate and render free of any third-party import, so only the pre-index path may ever touch tree-sitter.
components.depends_on: every verb module, imported lazily

evidence.why: the dependency firewall: only stdlib at top level, each subcommand imported inside its branch
_default_map supplies the conventional map path when no positional argument is given

deps.name: git
deps.type: version-control system, invoked read-only as a subprocess
deps.used_for: every file the viewer shows is read from the map's own commit; the pre-index reads churn; the impact engine reads diffs, rename maps and blobs on both sides of a range
deps.package: git (any recent version; a system binary, not a Python package)

evidence.why: the server's git envelope: no shell, timeouts, ref and path safety
the impact engine's own read-only git runner

deps.name: tree-sitter
deps.used_for: parsing non-Python sources for the pre-index's symbol index; a deliberate, scoped exception to the stdlib-only rule, confined to the pre-index path
deps.alternative: absent → the affected files are reported as uncovered, never silently counted as empty

evidence.why: imported lazily inside the pre-index, so no other command loads it

deps.name: tree-sitter language pack
deps.used_for: supplying the per-language grammar the pre-index needs to extract symbols outside Python
deps.alternative: a missing grammar makes those files uncovered rather than empty

evidence.why: get_language is how the pack supplies a grammar to the parser

deps.name: Mermaid
deps.used_for: drawing every diagram the view bundle emits as Mermaid source — flowcharts, class diagrams and sequence diagrams
deps.package: mermaid 11.15.0 (pinned in viewer.html with subresource integrity)

evidence.why: mermaid is the global the frontend renders through

deps.name: svg-pan-zoom
deps.used_for: wrapping each rendered diagram so a large map can be panned and zoomed instead of being shrunk to fit
deps.package: svg-pan-zoom 3.6.1 (pinned in viewer.html with subresource integrity)

evidence.why: loaded from the pinned CDN URL with an integrity hash

deps.name: jsDelivr CDN
deps.used_for: delivering the two pinned frontend bundles to the viewer page at load time; the page has no local fallback, so an outage breaks the diagrams

deps.used_for: the portable way to open a mapped source location when no local editor is configured — a blob URL pinned to the map's commit, derived from the repo's origin remote

evidence.why: the GitHub repo URL is derived from the origin remote and shipped in the view bundle

deps.type: desktop editor reached through its URL scheme (VS Code, Cursor, IntelliJ, or a custom scheme)
deps.used_for: opening a mapped file at its anchored line in the developer's own editor, from any box in the viewer
deps.alternative: no editor chosen or no local root confirmed → the GitHub blob URL is used instead

evidence.why: editorUri builds the scheme URL, or returns null when no editor or root is set

deps.type: per-origin key/value store in the browser
deps.used_for: remembering the viewer's per-machine preferences — the chosen editor, the confirmed local repo root, the GitHub repo, and the panel and pane sizes

evidence.why: the editor choice and custom scheme are global per machine, shared across every map

deps.name: Local filesystem
deps.type: plain JSON and markdown files on disk
deps.used_for: everything coyodex persists: the map model and its markdown view, the pre-index and provenance under the mapped repo's .coyodex/, the build fragments and reconcile file, and the server's recents list under the home directory

subdomains.name: Map model
subdomains.purpose: The committed map itself, element by element: the behavioral layer (roles, use cases, the Happy Path), the structural layer (subsystems, components, dependencies, entry points), the domain cards, the flows and backbone edges, and the operational tables. Everything here is serialized into one JSON document.

subdomains.name: Verification findings
subdomains.purpose: What the gates produce about a map: a source location parsed into a comparable shape, the drift verdict on a stored anchor, an audit finding, a grounding claim handed to a skeptic, and a proposed regrouping of an over-dense diagram.

subdomains.name: Structural pre-index
subdomains.purpose: What the code tree says about itself before anyone names a component: where each symbol is defined, which module a file imports, and how many components a directory subtree is expected to hold.

subdomains.name: Viewer graph & bundle
subdomains.purpose: The shapes the viewer renders rather than stores: the map flattened into nodes and edges, the per-project bundle of pre-rendered diagrams, the file tree with its coverage tags, one served project, and a parsed change report.

subdomains.name: Change impact
subdomains.purpose: How a git diff is expressed against a map: one diff hunk in the pin's coordinate frame, a file's affected line ranges, the anchors a change hits, and the options controlling how far the effect spreads.

subdomains.name: Method-quality eval
subdomains.purpose: How two builds of the same map are compared: the deterministic profile of one map, the semantic judge report over it, the thresholds and the gate, band and granularity results they produce, and the archived run.

subdomains.name: Build reconcile & provenance
subdomains.purpose: The two records that survive a rebuild: the declarative directives re-applied on every assemble, and the stamped history of which conversations produced a map.

subdomains.name: Behavioral layer
subdomains.purpose: Who the system is for and what they achieve with it: the roles, the ubiquitous language, the use cases and the ordered walk through them.

subdomains.name: Structural layer
subdomains.purpose: The machine: the grouped components, the external dependencies, the ways in, how to run it, and the citations that ground each claim.

subdomains.name: Domain cards
subdomains.purpose: The mapped project's own domain model as coyodex records it — an entity with its fields, its relations, where it is stored, and the types deliberately left out.

subdomains.name: Flows & edges
subdomains.purpose: How the parts interact: the per-use-case flows and their steps, the shared sub-flows, the one backbone edge list, and the async channel catalog.

subdomains.name: Operational & lifecycle tables
subdomains.purpose: The facts no diagram holds: processes and their environments, signals, security surfaces, configuration keys, the test gap table, lifecycles, and the recorded adjudications.

entities.name: ProjectModel

store.notes: one document per mapped repo, committed with the code; field order is the canonical key order so the file diffs cleanly

entities.meaning: the whole map of one codebase — its title and goal, the commit it is pinned to, and every element array

entities.name: Role

store.notes: one row of the map document's roles array

entities.meaning: a party the system is for — a first-class element other elements reference by id, never by name

relations.how: the use case names the role ids in its actors list, and the role restates them in its drives cell

entities.name: GlossaryRow

store.notes: one row of the map document's glossary array

entities.meaning: one term of the project's ubiquitous language, with the code home it is defined in — or none, for a pure product-level word

entities.name: UseCase

store.notes: one row of the map document's use_cases array

entities.meaning: one goal an actor achieves in a single run — its outside view, stated as what triggers it and what the actor ends up with

entities.name: HappyStep

store.notes: one row of the map document's happy_path array; order in the array is the walk

entities.meaning: one position in the ordered walk through the use cases, naming the use case it realizes and, optionally, the prerequisite that fixes it there

entities.name: Group

store.notes: one shape, two forests — the subsystems array and the subdomains array

entities.meaning: a subsystem or a subdomain: a named group whose membership is a single parent pointer carried on the child, so member lists are always derived

entities.name: Component

store.notes: one row of the map document's components array

entities.meaning: one module-sized unit of code: what it is for, where it lives, which files it owns, which process runs it, and the citations that ground the claims made about it

entities.name: Dep

store.notes: one row of the map document's deps array

entities.meaning: something outside the project the code talks to, described by two independent axes: where it lives (its kind, which decides whether it is drawn or folded away) and what it is for (its purpose bucket)

entities.name: RunRow

store.notes: one row of the map document's run_commands array

entities.meaning: one way to run, build or test the mapped project, anchored at the line that defines the command rather than a doc that mentions it

entities.name: EntryPoint

store.notes: one row of the map document's entry_points array

entities.meaning: one way into the system — a route, a command, a tool surface, or something that starts itself; carries who activates it and, when nobody outside does, when it runs

entities.name: Entity

store.notes: one row of the map document's entities array — a domain card

entities.meaning: one real named type in the mapped project's domain, read whole: what it means, where it is defined, its fields, its relations to other entities, where it is physically stored, and any lifecycle it implements

entities.name: EntityField

store.notes: embedded in its entity's card

entities.meaning: one attribute of a domain entity: its name, its type — a scalar or another entity — and the small controlled markers that say whether it is a key, nullable or a collection

entities.name: EntityRelation

store.notes: embedded in the source entity's card; authored on one side only

entities.meaning: one typed link from this entity to another, with its cardinality pair and either the storage key or the note that explains how a field-less link is actually wired

entities.name: Store

store.notes: embedded in its entity's card

entities.meaning: where an entity physically lives, structured rather than described: which dependency holds it, which compartment inside that dependency, how it relates to it, and what the shape cannot say

entities.name: NonEntityType

store.notes: one row of the map document's non_entity_types array

entities.meaning: a named type in the domain directories that is deliberately not modelled as an entity — a repository, a provider, an error — recorded so the coverage check does not count it as missed

entities.name: Flow

store.notes: one row of the map document's flows array; one flow per use case

entities.meaning: the inside view of one use case: the ordered interactions between the components, dependencies and entities it touches

entities.name: FlowStep

store.notes: embedded in its flow or sub-flow

entities.meaning: one interaction in a scenario — from one element to another, with its own action phrase and its own call site, or a reference that runs a shared sub-flow at this position

entities.name: SubFlow

store.notes: one row of the map document's subflows array

entities.meaning: a step sequence shared by two or more flows, defined once so every flow that rides it tells the same story at the same depth; it may not itself reference another sub-flow

entities.name: Edge

store.notes: one row of the map document's edges array — the single project-wide backbone list

entities.meaning: one relationship between components, dependencies and entities: a verb, the purpose the verb cannot carry, and a witness call site — or an explicit admission that there is no single call site

entities.name: MessagingRow

store.notes: one row of the map document's messaging array, keyed by channel name rather than an id

entities.meaning: one named channel, queue or topic — the async sibling of a backbone edge: which broker carries it, which components put messages on it and take them off, and what a message holds

entities.name: StateMachine

store.notes: embedded on the entity or component whose lifecycle it is

entities.meaning: a lifecycle the code actually implements — the declared state names, the transitions between them, and the line that declares them; never synthesized when the code has no named states

entities.name: StateTransition

store.notes: embedded in its state machine

entities.meaning: one move between two declared states, and the trigger that causes it

entities.name: DeploymentRow

store.notes: one row of the map document's deployment array

entities.meaning: one process the mapped system runs as: where it runs, how it is exposed, where its configuration comes from, and which environments it belongs to

entities.name: VariantTag

store.notes: embedded in its deployment row

entities.meaning: one environment placement of a process, together with the manifest line that grounds it — an empty source means the placement is inferred rather than proven

entities.name: ObservabilityRow

store.notes: one row of the map document's observability array

entities.meaning: one signal the system emits: where it comes from, where it is looked at, and what alerts on it

entities.name: SecurityRow

store.notes: one row of the map document's security array

entities.meaning: one surface someone can reach, who can reach it, the line that actually enforces the check, and what the residual risk is

entities.name: ConfigRow

store.notes: one row of the map document's config array

entities.meaning: one configuration key: what it is for, what it defaults to, and how it varies per environment — secrets by location, never by value

entities.name: TestRow

store.notes: one row of the map document's tests array

entities.meaning: one row of the test-completeness gap table: which map elements it assesses, whether they are covered, which suites exercise them, and what the remaining risk is

entities.name: ExtraSection

store.notes: one row of the map document's extras array

entities.meaning: a freeform authored section kept verbatim — and the place recorded adjudications live, where six specific headings are machine-read so a justified advisory goes quiet instead of re-firing forever

entities.name: EvidenceItem

store.notes: embedded on the component, dependency or test row that carries it

entities.meaning: one citation grounding a claim the map makes — the file and line a skeptic re-reads, and what it is supposed to show

entities.name: AnchorLoc

store.notes: parsed on demand from an anchor string; never stored

entities.meaning: a source anchor parsed into comparable parts — the path and, when the anchor carries them, the first and last line

entities.name: DriftResult

store.notes: computed per confirmed claim during the grounding reconcile

entities.meaning: the verdict on one stored anchor: whether it drifted, what it says today, the consensus line the skeptics actually found, and how far apart the two are

relations.how: both sides are parsed to anchor locations before the median line is compared

entities.name: Finding

store.notes: printed by the auditor; only the exit code persists

entities.meaning: one thing the audit noticed about a map — which check saw it, how serious it is, where in the map it sits, and what it says

entities.name: WorkItem

store.notes: emitted as the audit's L2 worklist, consumed by the grounding skeptics

entities.meaning: one 'what this actually does' claim a fresh-context skeptic must try to disprove, with the anchor to start from, why it is risky, and enough self-describing detail to find the code without the map

entities.name: HPStep

store.notes: the auditor's own reading of a Happy-Path step, built per run

entities.meaning: a Happy-Path step as the auditor sees it: its position in the walk plus the step ids its prerequisite refers to, which is what makes a forward reference detectable

relations.how: built one-for-one from the map's happy_path array at audit time

entities.name: Proposal

store.notes: printed by the balance report as a Direct-map-change block

entities.meaning: one suggested child group for an over-dense diagram — its name, whether that name came from a shared directory or from purpose, and the members that would move into it

entities.name: Symbol

store.notes: serialized into the pre-index's symbols index, by name; the extents feed the impact engine's symbol rung

entities.meaning: one class or function definition found in the code — its name and kind, the file and line it starts at, and the last line of its body

entities.name: ImportRef

store.notes: used only to compute the lower-bound import advisory between named components

entities.meaning: one import statement seen in a file — used as lower-bound evidence that one named component reaches another; absence is never evidence of no dependency

entities.name: DirExpectation

store.notes: serialized as the granularity block, whole-repo and per directory

entities.meaning: how many components one directory subtree is expected to hold, derived from the code alone; it has children only where the stop rule decided the directory was subsystem-shaped and recursed

entities.name: Node

store.notes: built from the model per request and cached with the served project

entities.meaning: one drawable box in the viewer — a component, dependency, entity or group flattened into a name, a source location, display fields, and the derived extras each diagram needs

entities.name: Edge (viewer)

store.notes: built from the model per request

entities.meaning: one drawable arrow — a backbone edge or a domain relation, carrying the cardinality, the resolved backing field and the note the info pane shows

entities.name: GraphDict

store.notes: the viewer's input, rebuilt from the model whenever the map file changes

entities.meaning: the whole map flattened for drawing: the header, every node and arrow, the Happy Path and flows, and the reference tables the diagram itself cannot hold

entities.name: TestRowView

store.notes: resolved server-side so the frontend needs no id parsing

entities.meaning: one row of the Tests tab with its targets already resolved to names and to whether each is a box the reader can be taken to

relations.how: one view row per stored test row, with element ids resolved to names and node-locatability

entities.name: HappyStep (viewer)

store.notes: the drawable form of a Happy-Path step

entities.meaning: one position in the drawn walk: it carries no story of its own, because drilling it opens the use case's flow

relations.how: built one-for-one from the map's happy_path array when the graph is assembled

entities.name: ViewBundle

store.notes: built once per map version and cached on the served project; also archived by the eval for inspection

entities.meaning: everything one project's frontend needs in a single payload — the merged graph plus every pre-rendered diagram, the crossing-edge lists behind each aggregated arrow, the flows as diagrams and as narratives, and the source-link configuration

entities.name: FileTreeNode

store.notes: built once per map version from git and cached on the served project

entities.meaning: one folder or file in the mapped repo, tagged by how the map covers it — so the browser doubles as a coverage view showing at a glance what the map describes and what it misses

entities.name: Project

store.notes: held in the running server's memory; the folder list behind it is what persists

entities.meaning: one served map: its URL slug, the repo it describes, the commit every git read is pinned to, and the lazily built artifacts dropped whenever the map file changes

relations.how: the project points at one project-map.json path and reloads it when its mtime changes

entities.name: DiffRow

store.notes: produced per request for the code view's inline diff

entities.meaning: one line of a rendered file diff — whether it is a separator, unchanged, added or removed, and its line number on each side

entities.name: Hunk

store.notes: parsed from git diff output per request

entities.meaning: one change block expressed in the pin's coordinate frame: which of the pin's lines it replaces, and what replaces them — its identity is what lets two diffs' fates be compared

entities.name: ParsedDiff

store.notes: one per file pair, per side

entities.meaning: one file pair's diff reduced to its hunks, or the fact that the file is binary

entities.name: FileFrame

store.notes: computed per changed file from the two side diffs

entities.meaning: what a change does to one file in the pin's frame: which of the pin's line ranges it affects, where content was inserted, and the honest special cases — no frame at all, binary, whitespace-only, or fully deleted

entities.name: AnchorRef

store.notes: the seed set, indexed from the model on every impact request

entities.meaning: one code anchor carried by a map element — which element and which of its fields, the path and lines, whether it claims a whole directory, and the component that owns it

entities.name: DirectHit

store.notes: one per anchor the change reached; the ripple seeds from exactly this set

entities.meaning: one map element a change reached directly, recording how it changed and — crucially — at which rung the match resolved, so the interface never shows more precision than it has

relations.how: each hit is one anchor matched against its file's frame at the finest rung that holds

entities.name: Change

store.notes: parsed from git name-status output

entities.meaning: one file's fate across a range — added, modified, deleted, renamed or copied — with both sides' paths when the file moved

entities.name: ImpactFile

store.notes: one per changed file in an impact run

entities.meaning: one changed file as the impact engine sees it: its name on the target side, the same file in the pin's frame, its fate, its frame, and the map elements it hit

entities.name: ImpactCore

store.notes: the projection layer's whole result, handed to the ripple layer

entities.meaning: one impact run before any spreading: the three commits it is expressed between, every changed file, and the warnings about anything it could not do exactly

entities.name: RippleOptions

store.notes: read from the request's query string; the noisy links default to off

entities.meaning: how far an effect is allowed to spread — whether read-only data links, the entity graph and the transitive call graph are followed, and how deep

entities.name: MapProfile

store.notes: written into each eval run directory and into the blessed baseline

entities.meaning: the deterministic quality signals of one built map — element counts, validator and audit outcomes, coverage, density, balance, flow granularity and the name sets a gate can watch — chosen so two runs of an LLM-authored map are still comparable

relations.how: built by loading one map document and running the shared validate and audit parse over it

entities.name: GroundingVerdict

store.notes: one per skeptic vote; only the aggregate survives into the judge report

entities.meaning: one skeptic's answer on one claim — held, refuted, or a failure that must never be scored as a refutation — with the evidence behind it

entities.name: RubricVerdict

store.notes: one per judge per dimension; the median is what is kept

entities.meaning: one judge's score for one rubric dimension, with the justification and the line it is grounded in

entities.name: DimensionScore

store.notes: embedded in the judge report

entities.meaning: one rubric dimension's settled score — the median of the judges' answers, plus how many judges answered

relations.how: the median of the N judges' scores for this dimension

entities.name: JudgeProtocol

store.notes: embedded in the judge report as its fingerprint

entities.meaning: which judging regime produced a set of scores — the pinned model, how many skeptics voted, how many claims were sampled, and a fingerprint of the rubric text and the prompt version; a mismatch invalidates a cached comparison instead of silently reusing it

entities.name: JudgeReport

store.notes: written beside the profile in each run directory and in the baseline

entities.meaning: the semantic half of a map's quality: how many risky claims survived the skeptics, the rubric medians and their overall mean, how many skeptics failed outright, and how many confirmed anchors turned out to have drifted

entities.name: Thresholds

store.notes: the committed starter file, merged with any per-project override

entities.meaning: the rules a comparison is judged by — the hard gates that block, the drift bands that only ask for a look, and the one band measured against the code rather than the baseline

entities.name: GateResult

store.notes: embedded in the delta report

entities.meaning: one hard gate's outcome — which gate, whether it held, and the numbers behind the answer

entities.name: BandResult

store.notes: embedded in the delta report

entities.meaning: one drift band's outcome — both sides' values, the signed change, what was allowed, and whether only a fall counts as a breach

entities.name: JudgeBand

store.notes: embedded in the delta report; empty unless both sides carry judge reports

entities.meaning: one semantic-quality band — how far the candidate's grounding pass-rate or rubric score fell against the baseline, and whether that fall was allowed

entities.name: GranularityResult

store.notes: embedded in the delta report; absent when no side was scored with the repo

entities.meaning: both maps' distance from the same code-derived component expectation — reported for each, but gating only on the candidate, because the baseline's own zoom may itself be wrong

entities.name: DeltaReport

store.notes: written into each run directory next to the profile and judge report

entities.meaning: the whole comparison of a candidate against the baseline — the verdict, every gate and band it applied, and the notes that inform without ever gating

relations.how: the thresholds are an input to the comparison, not stored in its output

entities.name: RunResult

store.notes: the in-memory result; its three parts are what get archived

entities.meaning: one eval run of one project — the map's profile, its judge report, the comparison against the baseline, and the verdict that carries into the exit code

entities.name: SetDirective

store.notes: embedded in the reconcile file's set array

entities.meaning: one bulk assignment applied after every merge — which elements, and which of grouping, runtime placement or purpose bucket to set on them; on the list field it replaces rather than appends, so re-running changes nothing

entities.name: DropEdgeDirective

store.notes: embedded in the reconcile file's drop_edges array

entities.meaning: one refuted backbone edge to remove on every assemble, and what to do with the flow steps that rode it — report them, drop them, or repoint them somewhere else

entities.name: Reconcile

store.notes: kept outside the fragments folder so the fragment glob never sweeps it

entities.meaning: the declarative build-time directives applied after the merge and before the write, so a re-assemble always re-applies them instead of silently reverting a whole synthesis pass

entities.name: SessionEntry

store.notes: embedded in the provenance record's sessions array; re-stamping the same session updates its entry

entities.meaning: one conversation that built or accepted a map — its session id, the minute it finished, what it was doing, and the code commit it was working against

entities.name: Provenance

store.notes: committed with the map so a backup can find the transcripts deterministically later

entities.meaning: the record of which conversations produced a map, so the map can later be bundled with the exact reasoning behind it

non_entity_types.name: ModelError
non_entity_types.why: an exception carrying the JSON path of a shape violation — error plumbing, not a domain concept

non_entity_types.name: ReconcileError
non_entity_types.why: the reconcile loader's own exception type

non_entity_types.name: Judge
non_entity_types.why: the dependency-injection boundary to the model — a protocol, not data; a fake implements it in tests and a sub-agent-backed one in the orchestrator

non_entity_types.name: PrecomputedJudge
non_entity_types.why: an adapter that replays verdicts an orchestrator already collected

non_entity_types.name: RecentsStore
non_entity_types.why: the repository over the served-folders file; the data it holds is a bare list of paths with no named type

non_entity_types.name: Handler
non_entity_types.why: the HTTP request handler — the server's routing plumbing

non_entity_types.name: _Maps
non_entity_types.why: lookup indexes built once per impact call from the model, not a stored shape

non_entity_types.name: _Impact
non_entity_types.why: the ripple layer's working accumulator for one element, flattened into the response payload

steps.phrase: clones the coyodex repo and runs `make install` from its root
creates the repo-local virtualenv if it is not there yet
steps.note: fails fast with a readable message when python3 is missing or too old

steps.phrase: installs both packages editable into that virtualenv, with the pre-index extra
steps.note: editable, so the clone stays the source of truth and docs evolve without reinstalling

steps.phrase: writes a SKILL.md into each agent's skills home with this clone's absolute path substituted for the placeholder
the installed manifest points the agent at the method's dispatch doc, which stays in the clone
reports the home each skill landed under, and the clone it points back at
runs `coyodex preindex --root <repo>` after drafting the behavioral layer
routes to the pre-index, the one code path allowed to load a third-party parser
asks git for each file's change count, to weight the tree by churn as well as size
records every class and function definition it finds with its file, line and extent
steps.note: Python through the standard library's own parser; other languages only when the grammar pack is installed

steps.phrase: asks the language pack for the grammar of each non-Python language it meets
computes how many components each directory subtree should hold, recursing only where a directory is subsystem-shaped
writes the weight tree, symbols, granularity and coverage blocks as one committed JSON file
prints the heaviest directories, the totals and the expectation on stderr, with the reminder to reconcile rather than copy
runs `coyodex lint-fragment --repo <repo>` on the fragment it is about to return
routes to the fragment linter
loads the fragment as a partial model, so a bad id shape dies here rather than a phase later
reuses the validator's own anchor-format check at fragment scope
reuses the validator's edge rules, so a witness-less edge is caught in the agent's own turn
confirms every anchored file really exists under the given repo root
steps.note: this is what catches a wrong repo-root prefix at the source

steps.phrase: prints every finding in one pass, and separates advisory warnings from failures
runs `coyodex assemble` over the clean fragments, with the reconcile file
routes to the assembler
reads each fragment and validates it alone, so a malformed one fails by name instead of poisoning the batch
merges the fragments into one model, refusing a duplicate id across two agents rather than silently overwriting
strips any backbone edge that names an actor, and collapses edges two agents wrote at the same call site
steps.note: an actor edge is a trace-prompt defect, so the count is reported as a warning to fix at the source

steps.phrase: asks which entity flow-steps no backbone edge covers
creates the missing component-to-entity edge each of those steps implies, inferring the verb from the step's leading word
steps.note: anything not clearly a write becomes a read, so a derived edge never invents ownership

steps.phrase: loads the declarative reconcile directives and applies them after the merge
steps.note: run after the edge derivation, so a dropped entity edge is not re-derived in the same pass

steps.phrase: writes the merged model through the one canonical serializer
renders the markdown view beside it so the readable copy never lags the model
registers the freshly built project so it appears on the map server's landing page
prints one self-describing digest of the resulting inventory and every mutation this assemble made
runs `coyodex validate --check-sources --check-coverage`
routes to the validator
loads the model
checks the semantics the loader cannot: every referenced id resolves, groups nest without cycles, steps carry a phrase and a site, edges carry a witness
reads each anchored file to confirm it exists, and each entity's source to reject a name with no real named type behind it
re-measures the tree itself for the component-count expectation, never reading the pre-index's own answer
steps.note: generation and verification share code but never data

steps.phrase: appends the always-on diagram fan-out advisories
reads the recorded adjudications, so a justified advisory goes quiet instead of re-firing forever
prints the blocking problems and the advisory warnings separately, and fails the exit code only on the former
runs `coyodex audit` on a map that already validates
routes to the auditor
loads the model
reads each Happy-Path step's position and the step ids its prerequisite refers to
steps.note: this is what makes a forward reference detectable at all

steps.phrase: makes the narrative order and the mechanism refute each other, and records what disagrees
builds the ranked worklist of claims no deterministic check can settle, most dangerous first
steps.note: each item carries enough self-describing detail that a skeptic needs no map file

steps.phrase: prints the findings and the worklist, blocking only on a hard prerequisite contradiction
runs `coyodex anchor-drift` with the skeptics' verdicts file
routes to the grounding reconcile
loads the model
rebuilds the same worklist the skeptics were given, so each verdict pairs back to its claim
asks the shared anchor helper whether the reported line drifts from the stored one
records the verdict from the median line the skeptics reported, so one stray skeptic cannot move an anchor
steps.note: one stray skeptic cannot move an anchor; a different file is always drift

steps.phrase: prints the drift worklist — it flags, the reconciler decides
runs `coyodex fix apply-drift` to write the corrections in
rewrites each drifted edge's witness line, matching on the whole source, verb and target triple so paired edges never swap
writes the edited model back through the one canonical serializer, never by hand

tests_note: Tests run for this table? YES — `.venv/bin/pytest tests eval/tests` was run during this build and all 807 tests passed. Coverage was NOT measured: no coverage tool is installed in the repo's dev extra, so which lines actually ran is unknown. Every row below is therefore judged by READING the suite and confirming it executes, which puts it at INFERRED on the confidence ladder — running with line and branch coverage is what would make a row verified. The gaps are the deliverable: the backup script and the browser frontend are the two large unexercised surfaces.

tests.label: Provenance stamping & map backup
tests.gap: The largest untested surface: 631 lines with no test file anywhere in either suite. Nothing exercises the provenance round-trip, the recovery path that finds a session by searching transcripts that wrote a map, the copy-versus-move rule that must never move a live transcript, or the destructive default of MOVING the .coyodex files out of the source repo. A defect here loses a map or a conversation, and both are irreversible.

tests.label: Viewer frontend behaviour

tests.why: a `node --check` syntax gate over the bundle — it parses the file without executing any of it, and skips entirely when node is not installed

tests.gap: 6,886 lines of hand-edited browser JavaScript with no behavioural test at all: the diagram click bridge, the drill history, the code viewer, the impact overlay and the editor hand-off are all unexercised. The one guard catches an unbalanced brace, nothing more — and it is skipped rather than failed on a machine without node, so the gate can be silently absent. Every viewer regression has to be caught by hand in a browser.

tests.label: Install and start
tests.gap: Nothing exercises `make install` or `make start`. The path substitution that bakes this clone's absolute path into each installed manifest is the single point of failure for the whole product — a wrong path makes every `/coyodex` invocation read the wrong method — and it is checked only by a maintainer running the install by hand.

tests.why: drives the static and view routes over a real socket
an edited map is picked up on the next request, a broken edit keeps serving the old bundle and retries
the working-tree read refuses ignored files, git internals, a relative escape and a symlink out of the repo

tests.gap: The loopback Host guard and the relative-path guard are unit-tested, but two guards on the same surface are not exercised end to end: the CSRF header check on the three state-changing POST routes has no test that a request without the header is refused, and the git ref shape check has no test of its own. Both are security guards on a server that has no authentication behind them.

tests.why: the weight walk, the Python symbol and import extraction, and the coverage block
the component expectation E and the stop rule that decides where to recurse

tests.gap: The Python path is well covered because it uses the standard library's own parser. The tree-sitter path — the whole reason the optional dependency exists — is exercised only where the grammar pack happens to be installed, so a polyglot repo's symbol extraction can break without any test noticing.

extras.heading: Entry-point coverage
extras.body:
cli: complete — walked the `coyodex` dispatch table (tools/coyodex/cli.py:76-108), the `coyodex-eval` dispatch table (eval/tools/coyodex_eval/cli.py), the two `python -m` debug mains, and map_backup's argparse subcommands.
http-route: complete — walked Handler.do_GET and Handler.do_POST plus both sub-routers (tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:511-682); every reachable path is listed.
agent-skill: complete — the two manifests `make install` / `make install-eval` copy into the agents' skills homes.

extras.heading: Self-starting entry points
extras.body: There are none, asserted rather than assumed. coyodex has no scheduled job, worker, poller, queue consumer, boot hook or signal handler: a search for threads, timers, event loops and exit hooks across both packages finds only the map server's own accept loop, which is started by the `coyodex serve` verb (tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:734) and therefore belongs to that external entry point. The server keeps itself in step with an edited map lazily, per request (tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:136), rather than by watching the filesystem, so there is no background watcher either.

extras.heading: Balance exceptions
extras.body: granularity: the map carries 22 components against a code-derived expectation E of 11 (band 6–16). E sizes a directory by mass, so it folds `tools/coyodex/`'s 37 modules into about nine boxes. Here that would hide exactly what the map exists to explain: each module in this repo is one command verb or one pipeline stage, with its own tests and its own place in the build invariant, so validate, audit, balance and the anchor-drift reconcile would collapse into a single "checks" box. The map is deliberately one altitude finer than E, at roughly twice its count, and every component still obeys the leaf rule (each is at most three files and well under the line cap).

extras.heading: Happy Path coverage
extras.body:
UC16: looking an element up with `coyodex dump` is an orchestration and spelunking convenience the agent reaches for at any point, not a step in the product's story — placing it on the spine would suggest an ordering it does not have.
UC17: backing a map up with its conversation is a deliberate archival action taken long after a map is built, so it sits off the walk rather than inside it.

extras.heading: Persistence exceptions
extras.body:
C12: the map server's only write is the served-project list — a bare array of folder paths in one small JSON file, with no named type behind it. Synthesizing an entity for it would put a box on the domain diagram that no class backs.
C14: the render step writes the markdown view, which is a generated rendering of the map model rather than a stored type of its own; the model it renders is already owned by the assembler.
C15: the viewer's browser-storage writes are loose preference keys — a chosen editor, a confirmed root, pane sizes — set and read individually, with no record type grouping them.
C21: the installer's writes are the virtualenv and a path-substituted copy of a markdown manifest; neither is data the product models.
